subject: Recalibrating MAP & escrow wording after procurement hold
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-health.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Need to recalibrate timeline + escrow language after procurement hold

Mina —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Short version: procurement at Acme has put a temporary hold on vendor sign-offs while they finish an internal risk assessment. They expect the hold to last 7–10 business days. That means our originally planned go-live window (mid-July) looks unlikely unless we compress a few knobs.

We'd like to propose:
- A brief rebaseline of the MAP to reflect the hold (new acceptance target: 2028-08-03)
- Clarification on escrow/credit language — procurement's asking for narrower SLA credit triggers and an escrow schedule if we can’t meet the new acceptance window

I attached the procurement questions and our internal MAP spreadsheet for reference.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) agree to a modified MAP schedule; and 2) provide a short-form escrow commitment (not full legal escrow) we can share with procurement to unblock internal approvals?

If it helps, we can do a quick sync on Monday.

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Neill
Program Lead, Cloud Integrations
Acme Health

Attachments: procurement-questions-20280609.pdf, Acme_MAP_v3.xlsx

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Need to recalibrate timeline + escrow language after procurement hold

Liam —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the procurement packet. We're sympathetic to the internal review timeline. Short answers up front: yes on a MAP rebaseline; yes we can provide an escrow-style contingency wording suitable for procurement review (summary-level commitment rather than full third-party escrow).

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) We will update the MAP to reflect a provisional acceptance date of 2028-08-03 and add a gated rollback plan if the procurement hold extends beyond two weeks.
2) We'll prepare a one-page "escrow-lite" commitment (technical artifacts + fallback model snapshot + contact matrix) that procurement can use while they complete their assessment. This will not include source code escrow — just an operational fallback package and cost-credit schedule.
3) Grace (cc'd) will draft the updated MAP with clear milestones and acceptance criteria; Karthik will propose a minimal SLA-credit schedule keyed to availability and mean-first-token latency breaches so procurement can evaluate the economics.

Can you confirm two things for us before we finalize the draft?
- Do you need the escrow-lite to include a retention/custodian name (i.e., legal counsel or vendor) or will procurement accept a Redwood-held operational package for the initial review?
- Is Acme willing to accept an acceptance-window buffer: if procurement clears within 10 business days we keep the original July cutover; otherwise the MAP moves to the provisional August date?

If you prefer a live call, I have 30–60 min available Monday 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: acme-escrow-redline.docx

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jun 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Need to recalibrate timeline + escrow language after procurement hold

Liam / Mina —

I started a compact MAP rebaseline and attached it as a worksheet tab in Acme_MAP_v3.xlsx (sheet: "Rebaseline-06-12"). Notes from my side:
- Acceptance criteria: add explicit eval plan items (3 workload prompts, latency percentile targets, and a throughput smoke test).
- If procurement wants an escrow-lite custodian, we can name an external custodian (recommended: legal counsel at "Riverton & Co.") — cost-neutral for the first 30 days.
- SLA credit schedule (draft): 5% credit if availability < 99.5% for two consecutive weeks; additional 2% per week down to a 10% cap. This is intentionally conservative for procurement review — Karthik, please flag any technical tradeoffs here.

Liam — quick ask: can you provide the names of the internal reviewers (security, legal, procurement) so we can map owners and reduce back-and-forth? Also, please confirm whether the hold is a hard stop or advisory — we treat hard stops as gating conditions.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

On a related note, I'm dropping a short decision matrix into the Drive link for transparency.

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-health.com, legal@acme-health.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jun 2028 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Need to recalibrate timeline + escrow language after procurement hold

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wants. To confirm:
- Hold is advisory but likely to be enforced by procurement leadership unless the risk package addresses two specific items (data residency mapping and an operational rollback plan).
- Reviewers: Nora Patel (Security), Tobias Reed (Legal), and Jenna Park (Procurement). Feel free to engage them directly — I've copied procurement and legal on this reply.
- Acme will accept Redwood-held escrow-lite for the initial review as long as there's a named custodian and a clear retrieval process. The external custodian option is fine if Redwood prefers it.

We're scheduling a procurement review for Wed (15 Jun) at 10:00am ET — would Redwood be able to join for 20–30 minutes to walk through the escrow-lite and the rebaseline? If so, please send an invite to the participants above and include the Drive link for the MAP revisions.

I'll also upload procurement's redline examples to the Drive folder by EOD.

Best,
Liam

Attachments: (will upload redline bundle to Drive)
